# `Browser.ScreenOrientation.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation.Internals — the low-level Screen Orientation
port surface: the closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js`
request/subscribe wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation` layer
wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:screen-orientation` axis
as the top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the
`Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation` path prefix), so the raw port surface cannot
be reached undisclosed.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type.

  * `Lock typeStr` — call `screen.orientation.lock(typeStr)`.
  * `Unlock` — call `screen.orientation.unlock()`.
  * `Query` — read `screen.orientation.type` once.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — deliberately NOT the app's internal
`Msg`. Every variant the browser can push is enumerated, so the fold in the
high-level layer is EXHAUSTIVE.

  * `Ok_` — a `Lock` or `Unlock` completed without error.
  * `Orientation typeStr` — the result of a `Query`, carrying the W3C type
    string (e.g. `"portrait-primary"`).
  * `Unavailable` — the Screen Orientation API is absent in this context.
  * `Denied` — the browser refused the lock request.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error JsMsg
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot `JsCmd` → `Task Error JsMsg`.
Routes through `Js.request` with the `inbound` decoder so the correlated
reply is decoded fail-closed by the same gate the `subscribe` path uses.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.
